Adventure left sensory HUD — current Windows executable source

Scope
  The screenshot's "Tracks Visible: 22" belongs to the sensory block of
  the main Adventure renderer. This block owns the spoor list, its eight
  bearings, the track counter and the strongest-odor field.
  The Freshest track popup is a different producer, retained separately
  in ../adventure-tracking/. Creature/quest compass badges likewise have
  their own producer in ../adventure-compass/.

Actual decompilation
  Input: /home/lulika/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Dwarf Fortress/Dwarf Fortress.exe
  PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  SHA-256: 205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7
  Ghidra 12.1.2, fresh import with -noanalysis, then the existing
  tools/DecompileAdventureMovementHUD.java script with current-image
  function, disassembly, call, literal and switch inputs.
  The complete renderer AF1190..B0390E and all listed suppliers were
  actually decompiled. pe-current-hud-ghidra.c is an unmodified excerpt
  of that new C output, with its source label and exit boundary retained.
  The full same-image renderer is also already retained at
  ../adventure-movement-hud/pe-reference-adventure-global-renderer.c.
  Each supplier has its complete C and assembly retained here.
  No running process or desktop was used for this source extraction.

All addresses below are reference PE RVAs.
  Owner: AF1190..B0390E
  Sensory eligibility/frame entry: AFEC59..AFED07
  Sensory frame continuation, list and labels: AFFC20..B0022F
  Track count append: 52C130..52C1E3
  Signed integer stream: 52C2B0..52C388
  Caste lookup: BBA90..BBADD
  Creature name: AA3BD0..AA3D93
  First-letter capitalization: 52D650..52D8BA

Eligibility and placement
  Display flags: uint32 at 2643BB8.
  If (flags & 5) == 0, this whole block produces nothing.
  flags & 1 enables tracks; flags & 4 independently enables odor.
  Mode word uint16 at 2640B70 must be zero to draw either text field.
  The spoor list can still be drawn when the mode hides the text fields.
  No alternate phrase is emitted by any of those suppression paths.

  A preceding compass/list moves the spoor frame down by ten rows.
  With a valid first spoor coordinate and tracks enabled, its 11x11 frame
  has top row 0 or 10, then the track counter starts at row 11 or 21.
  Otherwise the counter starts at row 1 or 11.
  The odor field uses the next row if the counter was drawn, or the same
  starting row if tracks are disabled.
  In the stacked case, native CP437 junctions replace the upper corners.

Spoor list
  Nine int16 coordinates begin at 2643BC0.
  First coordinate -30000 suppresses the entire list and frame.
  Within a visible list, coordinate -30000 skips that slot without
  incrementing the output row.
  Each slot's record has stride 16; its flags are at 2643C00-8+16*slot,
  and its type byte at 2643C00-6+16*slot.
  Native symbols are drawn at x=1; direction text is independently at x=3.

  Type 0: vegetation glyph '"' with green palette.
  Type 1: creature/caste glyph, falling back to '!' if absent.
  Type 2: item glyph, falling back to '[' if absent.
  Type 3: mess glyph '%'.
  Other types: no symbol. The independent direction branch still runs.
  These symbols are pictures, not English nouns.

  If !(record.flags & 2): no direction text.
  Otherwise selector = (record.flags & 0x1c) >> 2:
      0 N  -> 北       addchar call AFFE8E
      1 S  -> 南       addchar call AFFEA4
      2 E  -> 东       addchar call AFFEBA
      3 NE -> 东北     addst call AFFF3C
      4 W  -> 西       addchar call AFFED0
      5 NW -> 西北     addst call AFFF02
      6 SE -> 东南     addst call AFFFAA
      7 SW -> 西南     addst call AFFF73
  The one-character and two-character branches are equally semantic
  direction fields. Generic addst capture alone misses four of them.
  The runtime reader follows native slot order and flags, requires the
  current frame and exact visible bearing cells, and uses the existing
  Adventure compass vocabulary for all eight alternatives.

Track counter
  Count: signed int32 at 2643BBC.
  Count > 0 selects bright green; count <= 0 selects ordinary gray.
  Both branches draw exactly "Tracks Visible: " followed by the native
  integer. There is no singular, "No tracks", or special zero wording.
  Label call B00087 returns at B0008C.
  Number call B000C8 returns at B000CD.
  52C130 calls 52C2B0; the latter inserts a signed int into the native
  std::ostream and returns its string. Keep those bytes, without limits
  tied to the screenshot's 22 or a generated table of possible counts.
  Target: 可见踪迹：<native count>.

Strongest odor
  Race/caste/death state: 2643CCC / 2643CD0 / 2643CD4.
  Race == -1 selects ordinary gray; otherwise bright brown.
  Label call B00151 returns at B00156, independently of value call
  B0021C (return B00221).

  if race == -1:
      value = "None"
  else if death != 0:
      value = "Death"
  else:
      caste = lookup(int16(race), int16(caste))
      if caste != null and !caste.ODOR_STRING.empty():
          value = caste.ODOR_STRING at caste+0x4270
      else:
          value = creature_name(int16(race), plural=false, caste=-1)
  capitalize_first_eligible_letter(value)
  draw(value)

  The name helper therefore uses creature NAME[0], not CASTE_NAME,
  a personal name or a juvenile-name branch. Out-of-range/negative race
  or an empty NAME[0] can return an empty string; the label remains.
  The complete supplier C includes its other plural/caste branches,
  but this caller explicitly disables them.
  Capitalization skips bracketed markup and changes only the first
  eligible letter; "bug innards" becomes "Bug innards".

  Complete finite standard fields:
      Strongest Odor: None                 最强气味：无
      Strongest Odor: Death                最强气味：死亡
      Strongest Odor: Blood                最强气味：血液
      Strongest Odor: Smoke                最强气味：烟雾
      Strongest Odor: Mud                  最强气味：淤泥
      Strongest Odor: Bug innards          最强气味：昆虫内脏
      Strongest Odor: Cooked flesh         最强气味：熟肉
      Strongest Odor: Filth                最强气味：污垢
      Strongest Odor: Soot                 最强气味：烟灰
      Strongest Odor: Vomit                最强气味：呕吐物
      Strongest Odor: Soil                 最强气味：土壤
      Strongest Odor: Freshly-baked goods   最强气味：刚出炉的烘焙食品
      Strongest Odor: Brimstone            最强气味：硫磺
      Strongest Odor:                      最强气味：
  Death is shared by the native override and the RAW/procedural odor.
  All these complete fields already live in the runtime catalog.
  Strongest Odor: {s} supplies the complete term/creature grammar for
  dynamic NAME[0] and procedural names. Arbitrary mod-authored strings
  are open-ended; unresolved values remain verbatim with the Chinese label.

Runtime treatment
  src/adventure_tracking_hud.inc claims the actual native label/value
  writers before generic name and word matching. Adjacent draws are joined
  only when caller, row, grid, dimensions and current text agree.
  Both text layers and paired glyph rows use the same source ownership.
  Numbers retain the native representation; colors remain native.
  Eight-bearing fields use a four-cell layout, independent of the symbol.
  local-overrides.tsv and translations.tsv were edited in place.

Source inventory
  pe-current-hud.asm: every instruction in the sensory block's two regions.
  pe-branches.tsv / pe-conditions.tsv: native control-flow edges/operands.
  pe-literals.tsv / pe-calls.tsv: original string operands and suppliers.
  pe-switches.tsv: capitalization supplier's explicit switch targets.
  pe-ghidra-functions.tsv: full function bounds used for decompilation.
  raw-name-and-odor-sources.tsv: current installed RAW NAME/ODOR_STRING
  fields, and Lua odor-producing assignments, choices and propagation.
  Existing expanded creature vocabulary and its detailed provenance:
      ../adventure-smell/odor-raw-creature-name-sources.tsv
      ../adventure-smell/odor-raw-text-sources.tsv
  These are source extraction artifacts, not display observations.
